evidence_assessments.rationale: Multiple syntheses support an average explicit-instruction advantage on studied outcomes, but many samples/tasks are not Vietnamese near-A0 self-study and controlled outcome measures can favor explicitly accessible knowledge.

The complementarity conclusion triangulates several mature evidence families, but it is a cross-theory synthesis rather than a direct trial of one integrated self-study method for the target population.
Classroom meta-analytic evidence favors prompts on average for some outcomes, but feedback categories, targets and learner readiness vary; near-A0 AI-mediated self-study has not been directly tested.

Timing research suggests an immediate-feedback advantage in some task conditions, but the literature is comparatively sparse and definitions/treatments differ, making a global product timing rule premature.

The direction of the coverage-comprehension relationship is well supported for reading, while an exact 95/98 threshold is context- and criterion-dependent and the target population is not directly represented.
Each proposed content-selection dimension has support, but their integrated weighting has not been directly validated as a curriculum selector for Vietnamese near-A0 adults.
